title: Cabinet Refinishing in Dunnellon, FL | Vanities & Built-Ins
description: Cabinet refinishing in Dunnellon, FL for bath vanities, laundry cabinets, built-ins, and bookcases. Hard enamel finish and honest refinish-or-replace advice.
heroIntro: Bathroom vanities, laundry cabinets, built-in bookcases, and entertainment walls can all be refinished instead of replaced. Here is how we decide what is worth saving and how we finish it.

sections.h2: Cabinets are all over the house
body: When people think of cabinets they picture the kitchen, and we cover that in detail on our kitchen cabinet painting page for Dunnellon. But most homes have plenty of other cabinetry: bathroom vanities, a laundry wall, a linen closet, built-in bookcases beside a fireplace, a desk nook, or a media wall. Cabinet refinishing in Dunnellon, FL for these pieces uses the same finish system as a kitchen and is often the quickest way to make a bathroom or den feel current. It is part of the full list of work our Dunnellon painting team handles.

sections.h2: Refinish or replace? An honest checklist
body: Refinishing makes sense when the boxes are solid and the layout works. Replacement makes more sense when the problem is structural. Use this as a starting point:
bullets: Refinish: solid wood or plywood boxes, doors that close square, a layout you like
Refinish: laminate or thermofoil that is intact and not lifting
Replace: swollen particleboard from past leaks, especially under sinks
Replace: peeling thermofoil, or a layout that no longer fits how you use the room

sections.h2: Vanities in a humid river town
body: Bathroom cabinets in Dunnellon live in steady moisture. Toe kicks get splashed, doors around the sink take wet hands, and the interior of the sink base can stay damp. We check that base for soft or swollen material first, because no finish will fix that. Sound vanities are cleaned, sanded, primed with a bonding primer, and finished in a waterborne urethane enamel that cures hard and resists water. Good ventilation helps the finish last, and we will mention it if the bath fan is not doing its job.

Built-ins often carry old, yellowed finishes or stained wood that clashes with a newly painted room. They usually stay in place, so we mask surrounding walls and floors carefully, scuff and prime, and spray or brush the enamel depending on access. Shelves are finished so they do not stick to books and decor once cured. Laundry cabinets take a beating from detergent and humidity, and get the same durable enamel.
Already dealing with a failed paint job on cabinets? Our article on fixing peeling cabinet paint explains why it happens and what a proper redo involves.

Trying to match a vanity to an existing trim color? A removed door or a sample of the trim is enough for us to match it. If you are refinishing several rooms of cabinetry, keeping the same white or neutral across vanities and built-ins ties the house together. For more on our method see the main cabinet painting and refinishing service, or the deeper dive on refinishing versus replacing cabinets.

faqs.q: Can you refinish a bathroom vanity in Dunnellon?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the box is sound. Swollen or soft material under the sink is flagged during the walkthrough, since a finish cannot repair it.

faqs.q: Do built-in bookcases need to come out to be painted?
faqs.a: No. Built-ins are finished in place with the surrounding walls and floors masked and protected.
When the boxes are sound, refinishing avoids demolition, new cabinetry, and countertop work. We do not publish prices, but the estimate itemizes every piece so you can compare.
